title: Merchants stall before going live on PayTo
disclaimer: Practice scenario. The company is fictional and every figure is hypothetical. Australian market context is general.
company_context: PayNest (fictional) is an Australian payments provider that lets subscription businesses collect recurring payments through PayTo on the New Payments Platform.

brief.problem: Merchants sign up for PayNest but far fewer are going live with their first PayTo payment.
brief.objective: Lift 30-day merchant go-live from 38% to 60% within six months.
baseline: 30-day merchant go-live: 38%, down from 55% two quarters ago.
New merchant sign-ups: about 900 a month, steady.

facts.answer: A live merchant brings in about $1,600 a month in fees at maturity. The drop means about 150 fewer merchants going live each month — roughly $240k of monthly fee revenue per cohort at maturity, or about $2.9m a year.
facts.coach_tip: Size it, then say the 'so what': every monthly cohort compounds the loss.
facts.model_question: What's the revenue impact of fewer merchants going live?

facts.answer: Go-live means a merchant's first PayTo agreement is authorised by a customer and the first payment settles, within 30 days of sign-up.
facts.coach_tip: Knowing go-live needs a settled payment tells you to look at the whole setup journey.
facts.model_question: How exactly is go-live defined and measured?

facts.answer: About 900 merchants sign up a month. 70% are small subscription businesses like gyms, childcare and software; 30% are mid-size billers.
facts.coach_tip: The mix tells you where to segment next.
facts.model_question: What kinds of merchants sign up, and in what mix?

facts.answer: Small merchants: 30-day go-live fell from 52% to 31%. Mid-size billers: from 62% to 55%.
facts.coach_tip: Small merchants carry most of the drop — name that.
facts.model_question: Which merchant segments are driving the drop?

facts.answer: Median time from sign-up to the first agreement is now 19 days, up from 6. 41% of small merchants never create an agreement at all.
facts.coach_tip: Slower and stuck — look for the step where they stall.
facts.model_question: How long does it take merchants to create a first agreement now?

facts.answer: Last quarter: sign-up 100% → business verified 91% → bank account linked 84% → API or plugin connected 49% (was 78%) → first agreement authorised 41% → first payment settled 38%.
facts.coach_tip: The biggest drop is the integration step: 78% to 49%.
facts.model_question: Can I see the onboarding funnel, and where's the biggest drop?

facts.answer: Small merchants mostly connect through the no-code billing plugin for common platforms. Mid-size billers use the API with developer support.
facts.coach_tip: The plugin is the small-merchant path — that's where to look.
facts.model_question: How do different merchants connect to PayNest?

facts.answer: Two quarters ago the no-code plugin was replaced with a new version that makes merchants generate API keys and configure webhooks themselves. The old one-click connect was retired.
facts.coach_tip: Link the change to the integration drop before calling it the cause.
facts.model_question: Did anything change in the plugin or setup process?

facts.answer: New-merchant support tickets doubled to 1,300 a month. Themes: can't set up API keys 44%, webhook errors 27%, pricing questions 12%. Onboarding CSAT fell from 4.4 to 3.1 out of 5.
facts.coach_tip: Two themes cover 71% of tickets — your fix should target them.
facts.model_question: What are new merchants telling us in tickets and CSAT?

facts.answer: Pricing hasn't changed. A competitor ran a fee-free first month, but win/loss notes mention it in only 6% of lost deals.
facts.coach_tip: Good to rule out — it doesn't explain the timing.
facts.model_question: Could pricing or a competitor explain this?

facts.answer: Four onboarding specialists can do assisted setup, but their queue is 12 days long.
facts.coach_tip: Assisted setup is a lever, but it doesn't scale.
facts.model_question: Do we offer assisted setup, and what's the capacity?

facts.answer: Estimates: guided setup wizard with inline checks — 3 weeks. Restore one-click connect (OAuth) in the plugin — 6 weeks. Add 3 setup specialists — about $300k a year. PayTo requires the customer to authorise in their own banking app, so that step can't be removed.
facts.coach_tip: Map these to quick fix, medium and ongoing-cost options.
facts.model_question: What are our options and estimates to fix the setup step?

model_answer.problem_statement: Small subscription merchants are stalling at the integration step — plugin connection fell from 78% to 49% — because the new plugin makes them set up API keys and webhooks themselves, so 30-day go-live dropped from 55% to 38%, about 150 fewer live merchants a month.

options.name: Guided setup wizard
options.description: Step-by-step setup with inline checks for keys and webhooks.
options.business_impact: Cuts tickets; partial lift in connection.
options.why: Fast relief, but merchants still handle keys.

options.name: Restore one-click connect
options.description: OAuth connect in the plugin — no manual API keys or webhooks.
options.customer_impact: Connect in minutes, no technical skills.
options.business_impact: Targets 71% of tickets; could recover most of the 150 merchants a month.
options.why: Removes the root cause for small merchants.

options.name: Assisted setup team
options.description: Add 3 specialists to set up merchants for them.
options.customer_impact: A person does it for you.
options.business_impact: Quick help, but about $300k a year ongoing.

model_answer.decision: Ship the guided wizard in 3 weeks to cut errors now, and restore one-click connect within 6 weeks so small merchants never handle API keys.
model_answer.hypothesis: If we restore one-click connect for small merchants, plugin connection will rise from 49% to 75%+ and 30-day go-live from 38% to 55% within two quarters, because the drop started when one-click was retired and 71% of tickets cite API keys or webhooks.
model_answer.test: A/B test new small-merchant sign-ups: one-click connect vs the current plugin for 6 weeks.
